title: Protecting Resident Well-being amidst Commercial Activity
what_it_is: Protecting Resident Well-being amidst Commercial Activity

sections.label: Commercial activities in neighbourhoods
sections.summary: It highlights situations residents face from commercial activities in their neighbourhoods and how disamenities may be addressed while preserving liveability and business sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Rather, it seeks to highlight: one, the situations faced by residents arising from commercial activities in their neighbourhoods; and two, how these disamenities may be addressed in a way that preserves both liveability for residents and also sustainability for businesses, especially for responsible business operators who play by the rules.

sections.label: Neighbourhood enforcement and closures
sections.summary: A neighbourhood frequented by families saw enforcement actions close 10 massage and spa establishments offering illicit services after extended uncertainty and disruption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This is a neighbourhood which is frequented by families for enrichment classes and daily necessities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It was reported that recent enforcement actions resulted in the closure of 10 massage and spa establishments offering illicit services, but only after an extended period of uncertainty and disruption for our residents and nearby businesses alike.

sections.label: Number of exempted establishments
sections.summary: The number of such exempted establishments can run up to 2,000 today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Today, the number of such exempted establishments can run up to 2,000.

sections.label: Enforcement responsibilities across agencies
sections.summary: Enforcement responsibilities are often divided across agencies including licensing authorities, building management, environmental health and urban planning bodies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Enforcement responsibilities currently are often divided across agencies: licensing authorities for food, entertainment or massage; building management and estate maintenance; environmental health for noise or odour; and urban planning bodies.

sections.label: Refining planning categories for zoning
sections.summary: Planning categories can be refined to distinguish low-impact neighbourhood businesses from higher-impact uses such as late-night food and beverage, massage establishments, bars and karaoke outlets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For better zoning granularity, planning categories can be refined to better distinguish between low-impact neighbourhood businesses and higher-impact uses such as late-night food and beverage, massage establishments, bars and karaoke outlets.

sections.label: Good neighbour agreements for operators
sections.summary: For higher-impact uses, operators could enter a simple good neighbour agreement setting expectations on noise, waste, crowd control, solicitation and complaint responsiveness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For higher-impact uses, operators could enter into a simple good neighbour agreement setting out expectations on noise, waste management, crowd control, solicitation behaviour and responsiveness to complaints.

sections.label: Shared single case view
sections.summary: A shared single case view across agencies would let patterns be seen earlier instead of issues handled in isolation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A shared single case view across planning, licensing, environmental health, estate management and public order agencies would allow patterns to be seen earlier, rather than each issue being handled in reaction, in isolation.

sections.label: Transparent graduated enforcement framework
sections.summary: A transparent graduated framework would escalate consequences only when problems persist, up to licence suspension or revocation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A transparent, graduated framework would allow consequences to escalate only when problems persist – from tighter conditions or shorter renewal periods, to restrictions on hours or business activities and as a last resort, licence suspension or revocation.

sections.label: Residents seek clear rules
sections.summary: Residents seek clear rules, fair processes, early intervention and proportionate enforcement, not blanket bans or crackdowns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The residents that I and many of my colleagues here speak up for today are not calling for blanket bans or heavy-handed crackdowns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: They are asking for something far more modest: clear rules, fair processes, early intervention and proportionate enforcement, so that liveability is not eroded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Done well, the six proposals I suggested in this Adjournment Motion can benefit responsible operators by creating predictability, levelling the playing field and ensuring that those who cut corners do not impose hidden costs on our residents or on their better-run business counterparts nearby.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Speaker, a good city is not measured only by how lively it is at night, but by how liveable it remains at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As Singapore continues to intensify and mix uses more closely, our governance tools must evolve accordingly.

sections.label: Exclusion areas for new outlets
sections.summary: URA and SPF identified exclusion areas, including Jalan Besar, where new nightlife or massage establishments are not allowed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Responding to the Member’s point to look at local concentration of such outlets, the URA and SPF have identified exclusion areas, including Jalan Besar, where new nightlife or massage establishments are not allowed due to the high concentration of existing outlets and complaints from residents.

sections.label: HDB massage establishment quota
sections.summary: Since September 2024, HDB has tightened the quota of licensed massage establishments in HDB estates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since September 2024, HDB has tightened the quota of licensed massage establishments in HDB estates.

sections.label: Coffee shop outdoor area hours
sections.summary: HDB requires coffee shops to stop using outdoor refreshment areas by 11.00 pm to minimise noise.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For instance, to minimise noise, HDB requires coffee shops to stop the use of outdoor refreshment areas by 11.00 pm.

sections.label: Licence cancellation after warning letters
sections.summary: Three warning letters in total may lead authorities to cancel a licence or planning permission or refuse renewal.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: If a business operator gets three warning letters in total, the relevant authorities may cancel their licence or planning permission or refuse to renew it.

sections.label: Raids on massage establishments
sections.summary: After joint SPF and HDB raids, HDB and SPF worked with sold shop owners to evict close to 40 massage operators in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For example, following joint raids by SPF and HDB on massage establishments in HDB estates, HDB and SPF worked with sold shop owners to evict close to 40 massage establishment operators in 2025.

sections.label: Clearer information for applicants
sections.summary: Agencies will continue to look at making information clearer and more transparent upfront for applicants.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Agencies will continue to look at how to make these information clearer and more transparent upfront for applicants.

sections.label: Submitting COS cuts online
sections.summary: The online system for submitting COS cuts is operational, and Members are encouraged to start preparing and submitting cuts from today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Just before all of us go off, Members will be aware that we are approaching the annual Budget Statement and Committee of Supply (COS) Sittings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: So, I would like to take this opportunity to inform Members that the online system for submitting your COS cuts is already operational.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I would encourage Members to start preparing and submitting your COS cuts from today, using the online system.
